prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1062; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound through the intersection in League City, Texas, when the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, whose vehicle was southbound and entered the intersection against a steady signal. The impact was a side-on collision with significant force directed at the driver's door and rear quarter panel, and the damage visible on both vehicles is consistent with the reported mechanics of the crash. Driver 1 was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact and was assisted from the scene after reporting neck pain and stiffness. Passenger, who was seated in the front passenger seat, was also present, and both the responding officers and the statements gathered on scene confirm that Passenger was in the vehicle. Driver 1 described symptoms that fit the force of the collision, and the injury report is consistent with that account. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the vehicle positions and damage, but no independent witnesses were located who saw the collision itself. Records checked during the investigation show no prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle, and Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the applicable policy. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review of the signal timing.
